explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares LLM-as-a-judge (GPT-4) results with human evaluation results on the same set of instances, providing quantitative refusal rates from both methods and discussing discrepancies

prompts.notes: Full prompt provided verbatim in appendix section, including detailed rubric for three response types (full compliance, full refusal, partial refusal)

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: very high agreement across all models

guidelines.notes: Detailed taxonomy provided in main text §4.2 with examples, additional classification details in Appendix C

sample_size.notes: LLM and human both evaluated all 450 prompts (250 safe prompts and 200 unsafe prompts)

quantitative_scores.notes: Paper states 'the ranking of models based on manual evaluation is preserved by both string-match and GPT-4-based evaluation'

validation_results.summary_finding: Automated evaluation methods (including GPT-4-as-judge) qualitatively recover manual evaluation results, preserving model rankings despite discrepancies in exact refusal rates.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluators used identical three-category taxonomy for classifying responses
